children: The latest clearances cover an insecticide in Britain and a herbicide in Argentina, expanding the company’s overseas product portfolio

India Pesticides has secured regulatory approvals for its agrochemical products in the United Kingdom and Argentina, strengthening its international expansion plans and supporting prospects for higher exports.

The company said in an exchange filing on Tuesday that it had received technical equivalence approval in the UK for one of its insecticide products. It also obtained registration in Argentina for one of its herbicide products.

According to the company, the regulatory clearances mark significant milestones in its international growth journey and are expected to strengthen its presence in the global agrochemical market. India Pesticides added that the approvals could also support its export growth.

The latest approvals follow a technical equivalence approval received by India Pesticides in the European Union in July for one of its fungicide products. The company has continued to pursue regulatory clearances across overseas markets as part of its international expansion strategy.

The approvals in the UK and Argentina add to the company's regulatory presence across global markets and could provide additional opportunities for its agrochemical products. India Pesticides has been seeking to strengthen its international business alongside its domestic operations.

At the end of the June quarter, promoters held a 63.6 per cent stake in India Pesticides, while Foreign Institutional Investors held 2.52 per cent. Domestic institutional investors did not have any significant shareholding in the company during the quarter.

Public shareholders accounted for nearly 34 per cent of the company's ownership at the end of the June quarter. The shareholding pattern reflects continued promoter control of the agrochemical company.

Shares of India Pesticides gained 14.8 per cent to hit an intraday high of Rs 152.28 apiece on Wednesday following the company's disclosure about the latest regulatory approvals. The stock subsequently pared some of its gains but continued to trade higher during the session.

At around the reported level, the stock was trading nearly 6.2 per cent higher at Rs 140.90. Despite the day's gains, the shares remained close to their 52-week low of Rs 125 and were down nearly 20 per cent so far this year.
